profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer at UKG
profile.summary:
An interesting anecdote about my path to software engineering:

I worked in banking during the financial crisis of 2008 as an assistant branch manager for Washington Mutual. As part of the aftermath of the crisis, they were acquired by Chase. 

The industry shift and the overall experience highlighted the need for a change in career. I spent a few months exploring options and settled on a pursing a career as a paramedic. The expected time to complete the required studies was short and the industry was the complete opposite of where I was currently working.

While in training for my EMT license, which involved various ride-alongs with Miami-Dade Fire Department and hospital rotations; I realized that a field so close to death and illness was affecting my mental health significantly. The first time I gave CPR to a patient in cardiac arrest is a memory I'll never forget. I endured with the hopes it was something one could get used to and got my EMT certification and a job for a private company called American Ambulance while studying for my Paramedic certification.

My first two 12hr shifts resulted in no calls. I sat with the lead paramedic and seasoned EMT in an ambulance in the parking lot of a Best Buy for those two days, changing locations only for lunch, horrified with the sinking realization that this was not a sustainable career for me. 

On the third day, I downloaded Angry Birds on my iPhone to pass the time and vividly remember feeling so grateful for the escape it provided during those mind-numbing hours and I was possessed with the idea: "can I learn to build something like this?"

This lead me to resign from the company after finding a job that would not be as mentally intensive as the bank responsibilities were so that I can learn to code. I started a job at Public Storage as the facilities manager and began my tech journey in 2012. I immediately fell in love with it, programming. This eventually lead me to pursue a BA in Computer Science full-time in 2015, released my first iOS app in 2016, and was hired by Ultimate Software, now UKG, as a Software Engineer in 2018.

The iOS application I built as a student is still up in the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/keynote/id1085191030

Deciding to go back to school at 30 to pursue this career-path will forever be a pivotal moment in my life. "Am I really going to go back to school after a failed attempt at becoming a paramedic?" It remains the best decision I ever made.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description: Technical lead in UKG’s platform team; specifically leading the tream responsible for its eventing system

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Software Engineer on Platform Eventing team focused on seamless event propagation derived from data changes to our core product, UKG Pro, to downstream services spanning various product applications in the company portfolio. Currently working on modernizing the core monolith by enabling real-time Change Data Capture (CDC) on core SQLServers and streaming data changes with Kafka Connect Debezium Connectors as events to table specific data topics in Kafka.
- Developed JSON schema-generator for Java-based applications wrapped in a Maven plugin. Generator was annotation driven and produced schemas meeting company messaging standards from properly annotated POJOs representing events to be ingested by the organization's schema registry.
- Developed CLI tool in GoLang and Cobra to manage Kafka Connect Debezium connectors and associated SQL databases including enabling/disabling CDC, monitoring, creating, modifying and deleting connectors.
- Improved critical alert notifications for organization's legacy eventing application, replacing Sensu email-based alerting system with Slack based alerts driven by Telegraf, Influx, and Grafana. Worked with SRE to develop new processes which reduced response-times to critical issues from days to hours.
- Promoted to Software Engineer II after eight months in entry-level position.

positions.title: Facilities Manager
positions.description:
- Recruited by storage facility owner from my previous employer after seeing dramatic improvements in the property that I managed.
- Improved occupancy rate by 10% in my first six months.
- Increased net monthly profit by over 30% after discovering the previous manager was pocketing rent and adjusting the ledger as well as renting units listed as damaged.
- Left to pursue BA in Computer Science full-time at FIU

positions.title: Facilities Manager
positions.description:
- Managed storage facility of over 700 units in Downtown Miami including maintenance, sales, and audit preparation.
- Awarded Circle of Excellence for improving occupancy rate by 16% within my first four months.
- Reduced delinquent accounts by over 20% in an area notorious for its difficult customer base.
- Began learning how to code on my free time, started with Objective C learning to develop mobile applications for iOS

positions.title: Assistant Branch Manager
positions.description:
- Promoted from Teller to Operations Supervisor within six months.
- Passed all financial audits during my time as Operations Supervisor.
- Managed a team of ten tellers which included software training, sales coaching, cash box audits, hiring, and corrective actions.
- Promoted to Assistant Branch Manager after one year as Operations Supervisor.
- Managed a team of seven sales representatives and my replacement supervisor which included sales coaching, scheduling, courting high-balance clients, reviewing financial statements for loan applications, and corrective action
